name: security-certificate-revocation-policy-review
intent: Application certificate revocation checking and declared failure policy
artifacts: Actual TLS/signature client, OCSP/CRL behavior, cache/stapling and network failure policy.
trace: Trace whether the application checks revocation for the relevant trust decision and how revoked, unknown and unreachable outcomes differ.
experiment: Use an owned lab CA/client and synthetic certificates with controlled revocation responders; compare valid, revoked and unavailable states.
disproof: A missing network lookup can be explained by cache/stapling or platform policy; do not infer acceptance without the actual protected connection/operation.
repair: Enforce the declared revocation/failure contract and verify legitimate connectivity, revoked rejection and recovery.
branch_decisions: Determine the relying application policy for OCSP/CRL, stapling, cached status, freshness and network failure. Soft fail may be an explicit availability choice; a connection succeeding during lookup failure is not universally a bypass. Compare good, revoked and unavailable-status fixtures against the declared policy without contacting or revoking production certificates.
operational_method: Choose OCSP or CRL as actually consumed. For OCSP retain responder signer authorization, certificate/issuer identifier, status and thisUpdate/nextUpdate freshness under policy; for CRLs retain issuer, scope and update validity. Distinguish authenticated revoked/good results from unavailable or stale status and record the client failure rule. A tri-state fake responder establishes policy branching only, not verification of a real status artifact.
